transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-05-20 09:00 PT — Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood CSM); Maya (Acme SRE), Luca (Acme Infra), Nina (Acme Security)
Links referenced: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-deck (deck), https://sheets.example.com/benchmarks (benchmark spreadsheet)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i know we've got a fairly full agenda, we'll go through the network checks first then the perf numbers, and then action items, sound good?

[00:12] Maya (Acme SRE): yep sounds good, thanks. small note, we had a quick incident this morning with a route flapping while we were testing, so i'd like to confirm routing behavior end-to-end.

[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): ok, quick context — last week we validated VPC peering and private control plane connectivity. we saw the KV cache warmup working, and the control plane calls were stable, but there was the sporadic egress issue we discussed.

[00:40] Luca (Acme Infra): yeah that's the route flapping i mentioned, it looks like our NAT gateway had a brief failover and some connection resets hit the inference runner for maybe a minute. we captured logs, i posted them in the shared folder.

[01:00] Priya (Redwood SE): great, did the runner reconnect automatically? any cache loss?

[01:06] Luca (Acme Infra): reconnect yes; there was a small spike in cold starts and a few 5xxs while the KV cache was repopulating, p95 latency went from ~230ms to ~1.2s for those few minutes. we also saw ~0.4% error rate during the window.

[01:28] Alex (Redwood AE): ok that's helpful. for NAT failovers we typically recommend static egress IPs so firewall state doesn't depend on ephemeral source IPs — Sam i'll remind you to share the egress IPs template.

[01:40] Sam (Redwood CSM): yup will do, i'll include a firewall rules snippet and the recommended idle timeouts.

[01:47] Nina (Acme Security): on the security side, two asks: can we get sample audit logs with redactions? and confirm KMS integration for model keys — do you support HSM-backed KMS?

[02:00] Priya (Redwood SE): we do support customer KMS integration and can integrate with HSM-backed keys via the private control plane — i'll include the security deck and a sample audit log export in the follow-up.

[02:14] Nina (Acme Security): perfect, thanks. also need confirmation on retention policy options — 30 vs 90 days — what's standard?

[02:23] Alex (Redwood AE): typical pilot config is 30 days, enterprises often move to 90 days for compliance. we'll list the options in the doc.

[02:33] Priya (Redwood SE): moving to the routing checks — Luca you ran our routing test script? what did the results show?

[02:39] Luca (Acme Infra): ran it last night; most flows good but we noted asymmetric routing on one of the subnets, traffic out went through a different NAT causing stateful firewall drops. posted the pcap in the sheet.

[02:53] Alex (Redwood AE): ok that matches the route-flap symptoms. recommended fix is explicit route to Redwood egress range or using our static egress IPs behind your NAT. if you use a NAT fleet, ensure session stickiness or connection tracking timeout is >= our idle window.

[03:12] Maya (Acme SRE): what's the idle window threshold we should set?

[03:17] Priya (Redwood SE): we recommend at least 12 minutes for long-running streams; for short requests you can reduce, but 12m avoids KV cache TTL churn on reconnections.

[03:28] Luca (Acme Infra): noted. we'll test with 15 minutes and report back.

[03:35] Alex (Redwood AE): ok moving on to upgrades — Priya, you had a driver/kernel plan i think?

[03:41] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, we found one node in the cluster is on an older kernel and NVIDIA driver version which is causing GPU hang cases under heavy load. recommend scheduling a rolling upgrade: kernel 5.15 -> 6.1 and NVIDIA driver 535.xx, CUDA 12 runtime. we have a checklist: cordon, drain, upgrade driver, restart kubelet, verify GPU visible, run smoke test, then uncordon. should be low risk if you pick a maintenance window.

[04:10] Luca (Acme Infra): curious, any compatibility caveats with our current model runtime? we're using the quantized runtime build you provided last month.

[04:18] Priya (Redwood SE): we've validated the quant runtime on 535 drivers and CUDA12; older drivers showed occasional out-of-memory behavior under mixed batch loads. upgrading should reduce those OOM spikes and improve p95 slightly.

[04:32] Maya (Acme SRE): do you have a suggested canary percentage?

[04:36] Alex (Redwood AE): we typically start with 5% of traffic on the canary binary and watch p50/p95 and error rates for 2 hours, then 20% for 4 hours before full rollout. for POC you can do time-boxed canaries rather than traffic percent if easier.

[04:53] Priya (Redwood SE): note: if you see KV cache warmup regressions post-upgrade, enable the debug traces and we'll review them together.

[05:02] Luca (Acme Infra): ok we'll plan the upgrade for next Tuesday night, need to coordinate with our on-call.

[05:08] Alex (Redwood AE): next, perf numbers — Sam, can you summarize the benchmark from last run?

[05:13] Sam (Redwood CSM): sure; baseline (pre-tuning) p95 was ~320ms and token cost was estimated at $0.0012 per output-token for the workload in the sheet. after adjusting batching and enabling KV cache we saw p95 drop to ~230ms and estimated token cost down to $0.0009. with the driver upgrade and kernel tuning we expect another ~10-15% p95 improvement.

[05:37] Maya (Acme SRE): those numbers look good. during the NAT failover window though the latency spikes were worrying for our SLAs — we need a mitigation plan besides static IPs.

[05:48] Priya (Redwood SE): mitigation: use our local retry/backoff policy in the runner and enable request-level retries with idempotency tokens; also ensure the session stickiness and cache TTL recommendations. we can push a config change centrally for your cluster if you want.

[06:05] Luca (Acme Infra): please do that, push it to our staging first. also i'd like to run the routing test with the new idle timeout before the upgrade.

[06:12] Alex (Redwood AE): good plan. on the observability side we added tracing hooks into the runner; if you enable them we can map traces to model versions and cache hits.

[06:24] Nina (Acme Security): quick Q: does Redwood store PII in logs by default? we need to make sure any redaction is automatic or we won't be able to accept full logs.

[06:33] Priya (Redwood SE): default is to not log full request payloads in audit exports; we can redact or only capture metadata (request id, model version, latency, error codes). we'll include the redaction options in the security doc.

[06:45] Maya (Acme SRE): ok, thanks.

[06:50] Alex (Redwood AE): wrapping up — recap of action items: Alex will send security deck and sample audit logs; Sam will send egress IP + firewall template; Priya will prepare driver upgrade checklist and coordinate window; Luca to run routing test and share pcap and results; Nina to confirm KMS details in thread. agreed?

[07:10] Luca (Acme Infra): agreed. one more ask — can we get a final benchmark run after upgrade and routing fixes so we can sign off?

[07:17] Sam (Redwood CSM): yes, after the infra upgrades we'll run a final benchmark with the production-like traffic pattern and share the sheet + a short summary.

[07:26] Alex (Redwood AE): ok we'll schedule that for the week after the upgrade. thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the docs and tickets.

[07:32] Maya (Acme SRE): thanks all, bye.

[07:34] (call ends)
